title: Gas Scheduler
segmentLong: Midstream — Commercial Gas Logistics, Capacity Optimization & Transmission Pipeline Balancing
setting: Gas Transmission Commercial Desk & Scheduling Operations Floor: Dedicated commercial-operational trading and logistics floor surrounded by multi-monitor displays streaming live pipeline Electronic Bulletin Boards (EBBs), SCADA electronic gas measurement (EGM) telemetry, electronic data interchange (EDI) confirmation feeds, and ETRM transaction portals.
governingStandards: North American Energy Standards Board (NAESB) / Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC)
agentFocus: Gas Nomination & Timely Cycle Assembly Sieve
headline: The Gas Scheduler governs the continuous, high-pressure movement of billions of cubic feet of natural gas across interstate and cross-border transmission networks, matching supply with market demand under rigid regulatory cycle deadlines. While commercial Energy Trading and Risk Management (ETRM) systems like OpenLink Endur, Allegro, or SAP S/4HANA Energy and specialized Transportation Management Systems (TMS) like Quorum TIPS / eFLOW or Trellis Energy store planned contract nominations, they operate as static transaction ledgers that offer zero automated decision support during live operational flow disruptions. In any operating gas transmission network, unexpected compressor station trips, sudden freeze-offs at upstream wellhead gathering meters, or severe cold-snap demand surges trigger emergency pipeline capacity cuts and Operational Flow Orders (OFOs). Schedulers face an immediate, high-stakes operational dilemma: miss a strict regulatory nomination confirmation cutoff deadline by minutes or miscalculate physical receipt-delivery balances, and the commercial portfolio suffers immediate pipeline capacity cuts, stranded gas, unserved power plant customers, and punitive non-compliance cash-out penalties (15 to50/MMBtu, escalating to 100,000 to500,000 per event). Schedulers spend exhausting hours manually logging into 15 to 30 disparate pipeline Electronic Bulletin Boards (EBBs), sifting unstructured constraint PDFs, and hand-calculating alternate delivery paths in personal spreadsheets. Deploying a dedicated 7-agent hyper-specialized scheduling squad saves 20.70 hours per operational logistics cycle, eliminating confirmation cutbacks, preventing OFO penalty triggers, and safeguarding gas delivery deliverability.

confidence.Pain Claims Cited: 10 of 10 pain claims supported by published FERC pipeline tariff rate filings, natural gas midstream industry whitepapers, and commercial transportation dispute records

role.oneLine: Governs daily and intraday natural gas nominations, confirmations, pipeline capacity bookings, and physical pathing across pipeline Electronic Bulletin Boards to match supply with market demand while preventing operational pipeline imbalances and cash-out penalties.
role.whyItMatters: Natural gas cannot be easily stored on the surface or spilled without catastrophic safety and hydraulic consequences on transmission pipelines. Missing a standardized confirmation cycle deadline or miscalculating receipt-delivery balances triggers immediate pipeline capacity cuts, fuel retention loss, severe Operational Flow Order (OFO) cash-out penalties (ranging from 15/MMBtu to50/MMBtu or upwards of 100,000 to500,000 per occurrence), or unserved commercial load at gas-fired power generation plants and industrial distribution city gates.

variants.name: LDC & Power Generation Gas Supply Scheduler

role.titleCheck: Standard industry titles include Gas Scheduler, Natural Gas Transportation Scheduler, Pipeline Scheduler, or Gas Logistics Specialist. Absorbs the adjacent role of Gas Balancing Analyst. Avoid confusing this role with a "Gas Trader" (who buys and sells gas commodity contracts) or a "Pipeline Controller" (who commands physical compressor valves and line pressure from a 24/7 hydraulic control console).

whereTheWorkHappens.Work Setting: Gas Commercial Transmission & Scheduling Floor: High-paced commercial operations desk equipped with 3–4 ultra-wide monitors displaying pipeline Electronic Bulletin Boards (EBBs), electronic data interchange (EDI) transaction feeds, SCADA telemetry, and weather forecasts.
whereTheWorkHappens.What They Can Reach: Pipeline Scheduling & Transportation Software (Quorum TIPS / eFLOW, Trellis Energy, OpenLink Endur, Allegro, SAP Energy), Interstate Pipeline EBB Portals (10 to 30 distinct web portals), SCADA flow monitors, and gas trading platforms (ICE, GasHub).
whereTheWorkHappens.Shift Pattern: Extended day shift (6:30 AM to 6:00 PM) structured around standardized NAESB/ENTSOG nomination cycle deadlines, with mandatory weekend duty rotations and 24/7 on-call availability for Intraday 3/Evening cycles and emergency Operational Flow Orders (OFOs).
whereTheWorkHappens.Where the Record Lives: Central ETRM/TMS database (Quorum TIPS, Trellis), pipeline Electronic Bulletin Board archives, NAESB standardized EDI confirmation notices (18 CFR § 284.12), and monthly pipeline imbalance statements.

standards.citation: North American Energy Standards Board, Wholesale Gas Quadrant (WGQ) Standard 1.3.2 — Nomination Timeline & Cycles (Codified by FERC at 18 CFR § 284.12; defines Timely, Evening, ID1, ID2, and ID3 nomination, confirmation, and scheduling deadlines).

Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, Coordination of the Scheduling Processes of Interstate Natural Gas Pipelines and Public Utilities, 18 CFR Part 284 (Docket No. RM14-2-000, Order No. 809; gas-electric harmonization timelines and intraday bumping rules).

European Network of Transmission System Operators for Gas, Network Code on Capacity Allocation Mechanisms (Regulation EU 2017/459) and Network Code on Gas Balancing of Transmission Networks (Regulation EU 312/2014) (European standardized capacity auctions, nomination cycles, and daily balancing regimes).

Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board, Access Code for Common Carrier or Contract Carrier Natural Gas Pipelines Regulations and Capacity Determination Regulations (Capacity booking, nomination procedure, gas quality conformity, and imbalance management).
International Organization for Standardization, ISO 15112: Natural gas — Energy determination (Custody transfer measurement, gross heating value and energy conversions, mass-to-energy balance).
American Gas Association, Measurement of Gas by Multipath Ultrasonic Meters and AGA Report No. 7 / Report No. 8 (Compressibility Factors of Natural Gas).

agents.name: Gas Nomination & Timely Cycle Assembly Sieve
agents.oneLine: Ingests daily deal capture tickets, counterparty supply purchase contracts, customer delivery orders, and transport entitlement rights to assemble standardized Timely Cycle nomination packages across pipeline EBBs.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 3.60 hours daily of manual cross-referencing between ETRM deal books, transport contracts, and multi-pipeline nomination portals before the rigid 13:00 CCT NAESB deadline.
agents.reads: Physical gas deal capture tickets from ETRM ledgers (daily volume, price index, delivery point), counterparty trade confirmations, customer delivery orders, and pipeline firm/interruptible transportation contract master files.
agents.does: 1. Cross-checks confirmed physical purchase volumes against scheduled customer delivery requirements for the upcoming gas day; 2. Validates contract Maximum Daily Quantity (MDQ) entitlements and fuel retention percentages across all designated pipeline paths; 3. Generates complete receipt-to-delivery nomination schedules conforming to NAESB WGQ Standard 1.3.2 standardized transaction sets; 4. Formats clean, validated nomination packages for automated electronic submission across multiple pipeline Electronic Bulletin Boards ahead of the 13:00 CCT cutoff.
agents.returns: Timely Cycle Nomination Manifest complete with pipeline receipt/delivery pathing, contract validation logs, and pre-submission audit flags.
agents.stopsAt: Authorizing uncommitted commercial spot purchases or altering contract primary delivery point rights without trader approval.
agents.failureModes: If nominated volume exceeds available contractual MDQ or if counterparty credit limits are breached, the agent immediately flags [Contract Entitlement Violation: Commercial Approval Required] and halts automated submission for that path.

agents.name: Interconnect Confirmation & MDQ Entitlement Sieve
agents.oneLine: Cross-validates upstream operator receipt nominations against downstream point operator confirmations, verifying Maximum Daily Quantity (MDQ) contract limits and line-item ranking to eliminate cycle confirmation cuts.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 3.15 hours per confirmation cycle of manual telephone/email confirmation checking and contract entitlement auditing before 16:30 CCT confirmation deadlines.
agents.reads: Pipeline Electronic Bulletin Board confirmation notices, Quick Response (NAESB 855) EDI transaction feeds, upstream interconnect operator scheduled flows, and downstream delivery point confirmation logs.
agents.does: 1. Compares upstream supply nominations against downstream point operator confirmations on every pipeline interconnect; 2. Evaluates confirmation discrepancies and applies tariff-mandated lesser quantity rules to forecast net scheduled flow; 3. Audits shipper line-item confirmation ranking priorities (e.g., cut sequence for secondary delivery points); 4. Issues proactive confirmation discrepancy alerts to operators and gas control desks prior to cycle confirmation closure.
agents.returns: Cycle Interconnect Confirmation Dossier detailing confirmed quantities, lesser-of-quantity cuts, shipper priority ranking impacts, and unmatched line items.
agents.stopsAt: Modifying agreed physical interconnect delivery point flow limits without pipeline operator authorization.
agents.failureModes: If a downstream operator confirms zero flow or slashes confirmed quantity below minimum required delivery for high-priority gas-fired power generation, the agent triggers an immediate [Critical Delivery Curtailment Alert: Emergency Human Intervention Mandated].

agents.name: Pipeline EBB Capacity Cut & Dynamic Re-Pathing Sieve
agents.oneLine: Evaluates pipeline Electronic Bulletin Board (EBB) capacity constraint notices, maintenance derates, and point proration cuts to formulate least-cost physical path re-allocations across alternate secondary receipt/delivery points.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 3.15 hours per constraint event of high-stress tariff math, transport path re-modeling, and capacity priority hierarchy evaluation during pipeline operational flow restrictions.
agents.reads: Pipeline Electronic Bulletin Board (EBB) critical notices, capacity limitation postings, scheduled maintenance derate schedules, primary/secondary delivery point tariffs, and alternate pipeline interconnect capacity ledgers.
agents.does: 1. Ingests and structures raw unstructured capacity cut notices posted across pipeline EBB portals; 2. Maps affected receipt/delivery points against the active commercial portfolio to quantify stranded gas volumes; 3. Evaluates tariff-based capacity allocation priority hierarchies (Firm Primary, Firm Secondary, Interruptible Secondary, Interruptible Out-of-Path); 4. Calculates optimal least-cost secondary re-routing paths across available alternative pipeline interconnects or swing receipt points.
agents.returns: Dynamic Capacity Cut Mitigation Plan containing stranded volume impacts, evaluated alternate physical paths, incremental transportation tariff costs, and ready-to-file re-nomination packages.
agents.stopsAt: Re-routing gas across commercial pipelines where the shipper holds no active transportation service agreement or credit backing.
agents.failureModes: If all alternative physical delivery points on the pipeline network are constrained to 100% capacity, the agent issues an escalated [Bottleneck Lockdown: No Viable Secondary Path — Commercial Supply Curtailment Mandatory].

agents.name: Intraday Re-Nomination & Bumping Optimization Sieve
agents.oneLine: Monitors intraday cycle deadlines (Evening, ID1, ID2, ID3), models firm vs. interruptible bumping rights, and optimizes nomination adjustments across secondary and interruptible transportation paths without stranding gas.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 2.70 hours daily of high-speed bumping vulnerability checks and last-minute intraday nomination re-drafting.
agents.reads: Intraday nomination cycle timelines (Evening at 18:00, ID1 at 10:00, ID2 at 14:30, ID3 at 19:00 CCT), pipeline bumping notices, elapsed-prorated-scheduled-quantity (EPSQ) flow limits, and real-time plant burn deviations.
agents.does: 1. Calculates allowable intraday nomination change limits based on elapsed-prorated-scheduled-quantity (EPSQ) flow rules; 2. Simulates pipeline bumping scenarios to predict whether firm nominations will successfully bump lower-priority interruptible shippers; 3. Formulates optimized intraday re-nomination packages to increase or decrease flow to match changing weather forecasts or power demand; 4. Validates that proposed Evening and Intraday cycle submissions protect existing firm transportation entitlements without triggering unbumping penalties.
agents.returns: Intraday Re-Nomination Strategy Package detailing EPSQ calculation thresholds, predicted bumping outcomes, and cycle submission schedules.
agents.stopsAt: Submitting non-bumpable intraday nominations during the Intraday 3 cycle that attempt to cut already-flowed gas.
agents.failureModes: If an intraday nomination violates pipeline elapsed-prorated-scheduled-quantity (EPSQ) constraints, the agent rejects the nomination draft and outputs [Tariff Invalidation: Nomination Exceeds Remaining Unflowed Hourly Capacity].

agents.name: SCADA Telemetry Variance & Real-Time Burn Imbalance Sieve
agents.oneLine: Integrates live SCADA electronic gas measurement (EGM) telemetry, power generation dispatch schedules, and industrial burn rates to calculate hourly flow variances against scheduled nominations, projecting end-of-day imbalance exposure.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 2.70 hours daily of manual meter-by-meter SCADA polling and spreadsheet burn tracking, alerting schedulers to unpredicted flow variances 8 to 12 hours before gas day close.
agents.reads: Real-time SCADA flow telemetry (hourly flowing volume, pressure, temperature, energy rates from Emerson FloBoss/SCADAPack meters), power plant gas-fired turbine heat-rate burn schedules, and pipeline scheduled flow records.
agents.does: 1. Ingests hourly electronic gas measurement telemetry across all active physical custody transfer delivery meters; 2. Tracks cumulative actual physical flow against scheduled nomination profiles on an hour-by-hour basis; 3. Projects 24-hour end-of-day gas burn and calculates projected pipeline imbalance volumes; 4. Generates automated operational warning alerts when hourly deviations exceed pipeline tolerance bands (+/- 5% or +/- 10%).
agents.returns: Real-Time Gas Burn & Imbalance Surveillance Dashboard displaying hourly flow trajectories, cumulative daily variance curves, and recommended re-nomination trim volumes.
agents.stopsAt: Directly commanding physical flow control valves or adjusting telemetry meter orifice plate calibration factors.
agents.failureModes: If projected daily burn variance breaches the pipeline operating tolerance threshold during an active Operational Flow Order (OFO), the agent triggers an immediate [Emergency Imbalance Warning: Severe OFO Cash-Out Exposure Imminent].

agents.name: Underground Gas Storage (UGS) & Park-and-Loan (PAL) Balancing Sieve
agents.oneLine: Reconciles working gas inventory balances, ratchet curves, minimum/maximum daily injection/withdrawal rights, and Park-and-Loan (PAL) service fees to schedule physical storage balancing and absorb unexpected supply swings.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 2.25 hours daily of storage ratchet curve lookups, inventory ceiling audits, and parking contract deadline tracking.
agents.reads: Underground storage (UGS) facility inventory ledgers, contractual injection/withdrawal ratchet schedules (flow capability vs. inventory level), pipeline Park-and-Loan (PAL) contract balances, and daily system imbalance projections.
agents.does: 1. Evaluates current storage inventory against operational minimum cushion gas and maximum working gas capacity limits; 2. Calculates maximum allowable daily withdrawal and injection rates based on dynamic reservoir pressure ratchet curves; 3. Formulates optimal storage injection or withdrawal nominations to offset projected pipeline physical imbalance deficits or surpluses; 4. Evaluates Park-and-Loan (PAL) parking and lending service fee schedules to minimize daily holding costs during temporary delivery disruptions.
agents.returns: Gas Storage & PAL Balancing Schedule detailing allowable injection/withdrawal nominations, ratchet constraints, inventory status, and economic parking recommendations.
agents.stopsAt: Authorizing physical storage withdrawals that violate mandatory cushion gas baseline reserves.
agents.failureModes: If a proposed storage withdrawal exceeds the contractual reservoir deliverability ratchet limit for the current inventory tier, the agent flags an immediate [Storage Ratchet Violation: Maximum Deliverability Exceeded — Volume Adjusted].

agents.name: Pipeline OFO, Imbalance Cash-Out & OBA Reconciliation Synthesizer
agents.oneLine: Ingests pipeline monthly actual allocated volumes, Operational Balancing Agreements (OBAs), Critical Peak OFO notices, and pipeline cash-out price indices to audit monthly transportation billing statements and resolve penalty disputes.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 3.15 hours per monthly billing and OFO event of forensic multi-tariff audit reconciliation, verifying tiered cash-out penalty formulas and contesting unjust pipeline imbalance charges.
agents.reads: Final pipeline monthly actual allocated volume statements, Operational Balancing Agreement (OBA) cumulative records, published pipeline monthly cash-out price index tables, and active Operational Flow Order (OFO) penalty logs.
agents.does: 1. Audits monthly actual allocated volumes against daily confirmed scheduled flows across every receipt and delivery point; 2. Applies complex tiered cash-out penalty formulas (e.g., 0-5% tolerance at index, 5-10% at 110% index, >20% at 150% index) to verify pipeline penalty billings; 3. Reconciles cumulative OBA balances between interconnected pipeline transmission operators; 4. Detects improper penalty assessments, erroneous meter allocation adjustments, or misapplied OFO non-performance surcharges, generating certified billing dispute dossiers.
agents.returns: Monthly Pipeline Transportation Reconciliation & Billing Audit Dossier complete with itemized cash-out verification sheets, penalty audit logs, and formal invoice dispute packages.
agents.stopsAt: Executing legal dispute settlements or signing commercial cash-out write-off authorizations.
agents.failureModes: If the agent detects an unannounced pipeline meter re-allocation that retroactively generates an unauthorized OFO penalty (> 50,000), the agent flags an immediate [Material Billing Anomaly: Formal Pipeline Tariff Dispute Package Assembled].

valueModel.rule: Quantify the unit of work. Never multiply into speculative enterprise rupee or dollar totals. The operating pipeline shipper provides its own gas throughput, transport tariff, and imbalance penalty rate multipliers.

negativeSearch.searched: Quorum Software (TIPS / eFLOW), Trellis Energy, OpenLink Endur, and midstream conference proceedings for "autonomous dynamic pipeline capacity cut re-pathing across secondary delivery points integrating live multi-pipeline EBB notices with hydraulic flow models without manual scheduler re-entry".
negativeSearch.result: Negative Search, 2026-09. Commercial TMS and ETRM suites record nominations and log confirmation statuses; none continuously ingest live, unstructured multi-pipeline EBB cut notices to autonomously calculate least-cost dynamic re-routing across alternate secondary points and re-submit nomination schedules before NAESB cycle cutoff windows without human manual intervention.

line: "In natural gas transmission, missing a cycle deadline by ninety seconds does not mean an email goes unanswered — it means fifty thousand dekatherms of firm pipeline capacity are cut, a power plant is starved of generation fuel, and the commercial desk absorbs a hundred-thousand-dollar cash-out penalty before lunch."
openQuestions: How many hours per day does your scheduling desk spend manually logging into disparate pipeline Electronic Bulletin Boards (EBBs) to retrieve capacity cut notices and confirmation statuses?
What was the largest operational imbalance cash-out or non-performance penalty incurred by your commercial portfolio over the past winter heating or summer cooling season?
When a primary delivery point is constrained or cut by a transmission pipeline, how do you currently identify and calculate the least-cost secondary re-routing path before the cycle cutoff deadline?
